standard_prerequisites.use: Gross, Vector bundles as generators on schemes and stacks (Proposition 1.3.1, an ampleness criterion on blow-ups checked formally along the centre), the chapter's preceding blow-up/slice lemmas used inside the proof, and standard ampleness machinery on the generic fibre.

core_obligations: Reduce the ampleness check on the blow-up to the formal fibres along the centre.
Split into the two incidence cases of the centre with the special fibre.
Invoke the named earlier lemmas to construct the finite type ideal with the required support conditions.

proof_roadmap.step: Formal-fibre ampleness reduction via the cited Gross proposition.
Case split on incidence and ideal construction from the chapter's earlier lemmas.

difficulty_reason: For a proper flat finitely presented morphism X -> B of finite presentation with B a Dedekind domain, a closed subscheme Z -> X finite and of finite presentation over B, and a prime b of height 1 with the restriction of an invertible O_X-module L to the fibre X_b ample and L|_{Z_b} ample, the lemma produces the blow-up of X in a finite type ideal, contained in the closure of Z_b and disjoint from a general point of Z_b, after which L remains ample on the blown-up scheme restricted to the closure of the generic fibre of Z. The retained proof is written: it reduces to checking ampleness after the Gross-thesis proposition (cited by number in the statement) that ampleness on a blow-up can be checked on the formal fibres along the centre, splits into the two cases where the centre meets the special fibre or not, and in each case invokes the chapter's preceding lemmas building the ideal (More on Flatness input and the chapter's own slice machinery) with explicit references to the author's earlier lemmas; nothing is deferred to an omitted proof. Retained author proof at lines 23402-23438. The statement cites \cite[Proposition 1.3.1]{Gross-thesis}; a card-local bibliography.tex supplies the entry.

dedup.scope: Blow-up lemma producing a centre near a height-one prime preserving ampleness; unique aggregate statement.
